title: SPML Infra Ltd - 500402 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 53% YoY to INR293.9 crores with PAT up 140% to INR28 crores, but FY26 revenue of INR868 crores missed the INR900-1,000 crore guidance.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR293.9 crores, up 53% YoY and 27% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR25 crores at an 8.4% margin and PAT of INR28 crores. Management attributed the margin dip to one-time legal and arbitration costs, a non-cash expected credit loss provision and bank limit mobilisation costs. FY26 revenue of INR868 crores (up 13%), EBITDA of INR86 crores (9.7% margin) and PAT of INR76 crores (up 55%) fell short of the INR900-1,000 crore revenue guidance, which management blamed on fund-availability-linked execution pacing in March. Management guided to at least 25% growth in revenue and profit in FY27, and the company is building BESS manufacturing capacity alongside its water EPC business.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR299.55 crores; includes INR137 crores back-to-back debtors

financial_highlights.value: INR5,369 crores (about INR4,000 crores new, INR1,369 crores legacy)
INR380 crores against agreed INR700 crores

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Management said water is about 85-90% of revenue in the quarter and year; the company targets INR5,000 crores of total (incl. JV) order intake per year, with net share of INR2,500-3,000 crores. Recent wins include Kekri (Rajasthan, Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0), Indore (AMRUT) and Ranchi (NABARD).

segments.name: Power and BESS
segments.commentary: Power is a very small share of revenue. A 2.5 GWh BESS assembly line at Supa MIDC Pune is due to start by end-June 2026, expanding to 5 GW and 600 containerised units per year by end-2026. The NTPC BESS order is INR1,128 crores, of which INR96 crores is O&M; capex for BESS up to 5 GW plus containers is about INR200 crores plus INR35 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27: at least 25% growth in both top line and bottom line, with growth expected in every quarter; management said it will give annual numeric guidance at the annual call.
Shortfall in FY26 revenue (about INR50-100 crores of spillover) expected to be executed in Q1 and Q2 FY27; management said EPC orders execute over about 3 years.
EBITDA margin target of around 10%; new orders carry a minimum 10% margin, and management said the Q4 margin would have been about 10% without one-time costs.

NARCL: about INR45 crores minimum payment planned in FY27; surplus cash to be used for growth rather than NARCL repayment; arbitration awards in hand (about INR627-630 crores) expected to cover the balance.
Tax: accumulated losses and the new tax regime (no MAT) expected to keep tax payments low for a few years; management cited a tax shield of more than INR500 crores.
capex_capacity: 2.5 GWh BESS assembly line at Supa MIDC Pune to commence by end-June 2026, with expansion to 5 GW planned.
Container manufacturing of 600 units per year targeted by end-2026, for about INR35 crores.
Total BESS capex (up to 5 GW) about INR200 crores including about INR25 crores R&D; INR175 crores quoted for the 2.5 GW and 5 GW phases with INR125 crores for the first 2.5 GW.
Battery packs are about 35-40% of BESS EPC cost and containers about 8-10%, with battery packs and containers being manufactured in-house.
Peak revenue potential quoted as INR2,500 crores per 2.5 GW phase, about INR5,000 crores for both phases.
demand_pricing: Management cited government BESS targets of about 236 GW by 2031-32 and a 10% BESS mandate for renewables; it said 92 GW of BESS projects are in the pipeline.
All new contracts carry price variation clauses; management said it takes no order without PV and without clarity on funding.
Margin discipline: new orders are being taken at minimum 10% margin; OEM battery-pack orders also at minimum 10%.
Payment terms: NTPC and Power Grid BESS orders expected at 15-20 days; World Bank or bank-funded water projects 15-30 days.
Competition in BESS is rising; management pointed to its Energy Vault tie-up and power EPC experience as advantages.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue below the INR900-1,000 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution is linked to customer fund availability; March saw customer fund shortfalls on tenders such as RITES, so about INR50-100 crores of spillover moves into FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins dip in Q4 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited one-time legal and arbitration costs, an Ind AS expected credit loss provision and bank limit mobilisation costs, together adding about INR10 crores to other expenses; margin is expected to rise as new orders grow in the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net water order book and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is INR5,000 crores total order intake per year including JVs, with net share of INR2,500-3,000 crores; the analyst's net order book estimate was about INR3,300 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Are Jal Jeevan Mission payment delays a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JJM payments were stopped for verification and are resuming, with the scheme extended to 2028; it has not taken new JJM projects recently and is focused on AMRUT and bank-funded projects.

qa_highlights.question: How will the NARCL dues be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR630 crores of awards are in hand, with about 75% payable to NARCL; the balance is expected to be funded from awards rather than operating cash flow, with about INR380 crores to be paid in total.

risks_watch: FY26 revenue missed the INR900-1,000 crore guidance; the spillover of INR50-100 crores into FY27 must show up in Q1 and Q2 results.
Dependence on customer fund flows and government payments; JJM payment delays were acknowledged, and the company said it is avoiding orders without funding clarity.
NARCL repayment depends on arbitration awards, with about INR4,526 crores of claims pending and historical conversion of about 40%.
Net debt to EBITDA of 4.41x, debt-to-equity of 0.4x, receivables of INR417.5 crores and surety bond exposure of INR305 crores.
Q4 PAT includes a tax reversal from recognised accumulated losses; sustainability of earnings depends on this and on the 10% margin target.
BESS commissioning by end-June 2026 and 5 GW expansion by year-end; watch for timing slippage and the margin on OEM and EPC orders.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and FY27 growth (at least 25%), but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss, which management attributed to fund timing. Answers on the NARCL repayment and arbitration award conversion were detailed but internally inconsistent on figures, and several answers on the order book and BESS capacity were vague.
key_quotes: The company has decided to remain focused on execution rather than building the order book and will remain very selective in choosing orders given the enormous opportunity currently available across all sectors the company deals with.
So unless there is a PV, we don't take the order.
The management remains focused and committed to deliver on its guidance, and we are optimistic about what lies ahead for the SPML Infra.
